Get Loopar running with a single command:

```bash
npx loopar-install my-project --port 8080
```

The installer:

1. Clones the Loopar framework
2. Installs every dependency with Yarn (PM2 comes with them — no global install)
3. Creates the default **dev** site
4. Opens the **TUI** (the terminal tenant manager), which starts the Loopar core

Then open the URL the TUI shows (press `o`), for example:

```
http://localhost:8080
```

The **install wizard** asks for your database, your organization and the Administrator account. When it finishes you land in the **Desk** — Loopar's visual development environment.

> **How it runs:** Loopar runs as **one Node process, the core**. Every site (tenant) is served from that process, each with its own database, configuration and domain. PM2 keeps the core alive; Caddy routes every tenant domain to it and handles SSL.
"},"imageProps":{},"style":{}},{"element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Prerequisites","key":"md_prerequisites","id":"prerequisites","name":"md_prerequisites","value":"# Prerequisites

Before installing Loopar, ensure your system meets the following requirements:

---

## Required

| Requirement | Version | Notes |
|-------------|---------|-------|
| **Node.js** | 22.22+ | Checked on install, by the CLI and when the core boots |
| **Yarn** | 4+ | **Required** — enabled through Corepack |

> ⚠️ **Important:** Loopar is a Yarn-workspaces monorepo and **requires Yarn 4+**. npm and pnpm are not supported and can cause dependency-resolution errors.

---

## Process Manager and Proxy

| Tool | Purpose | How you get it |
|------|---------|----------------|
| **PM2** | Keeps the core process alive | A project dependency — installed by `yarn install`. Loopar runs its own **project-local** daemon (`.pm2/`), so no global PM2 is needed |
| **Caddy** | Routes tenant domains to the core, automatic SSL | Installed on the system (see [Manual Dependencies Installation](#manual-dependencies)). Optional on a development machine |

---

## Database (one of the following)

| Database | Driver | Recommended For |
|----------|--------|----------------|
| MySQL / MariaDB | `mysql2` | Production environments |
| PostgreSQL | `pg` | Advanced features & scalability |
| SQLite | `better-sqlite3` | Development & small deployments |
| SQL Server | `tedious` | Microsoft-based infrastructure |
| Oracle | `oracledb` | Enterprise Oracle environments |

---

## Verify Your Environment

```bash
# Check Node.js version (must be 22.22+)
node --version

# Check Yarn version (must be 4+)
yarn --version
```

### Installing Node.js

If you need to install or update Node.js:

```bash
# Using nvm (recommended)
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.0/install.sh | bash
nvm install 22
nvm use 22
nvm alias default 22
```

Or visit [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/) for direct downloads.

### Enabling Yarn 4

Yarn 4 ships through Corepack, which is bundled with Node.js 16.9+:

```bash
# Enable Corepack (one time)
corepack enable

# Activate the latest stable Yarn
yarn set version stable

# Verify
yarn --version
# Should output: 4.x.x
```"},"imageProps":{},"style":{}},{"element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Installation","key":"md_installation","id":"installation","name":"md_installation","value":"# Installation

---

## Automatic Installation (Recommended)

One command does everything:

```bash
npx loopar-install my-project --port 8080
```

The installer will:

1. ✅ Clone the Loopar framework
2. ✅ Install all dependencies with Yarn
3. ✅ Create the default **dev** site
4. ✅ Open the TUI, which starts the core

Open the URL the TUI shows to continue with the install wizard.

---

## Manual Installation

For more control over the setup process, or if the automatic installation fails.

### 1. Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/alphabit-technology/loopar-framework.git my-project
cd my-project
```

### 2. Install Dependencies

```bash
yarn install
```

> ⚠️ **Important:** You must use **Yarn 4+** (enabled through Corepack). npm and pnpm are not supported — they corrupt `node_modules` and the lockfile.

`yarn install` checks your Node version and creates the `dev` site if it doesn't exist yet.

### 3. Start Loopar

```bash
yarn start
```

`yarn start` opens the **TUI** (interactive tenant manager) and starts the core if it is down. Press `o` (or click the URL) to open the site.

On a server without an interactive terminal, boot the core headless instead:

```bash
yarn serve
```

---

## Verify Installation

Open the URL in your browser:

```
http://localhost:3000
```

You should see the install wizard.
"},"imageProps":{},"style":{}},{"element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Manual Dependencies","key":"md_manual_dependencies","id":"manual-dependencies","name":"md_manual_dependencies","value":"# Manual Dependencies Installation

Caddy is a system package. Install it on servers that serve public domains (it is optional on a development machine).

---

## PM2

PM2 is a project dependency: `yarn install` brings it, and Loopar runs its own **project-local daemon** (state under `.pm2/` in the project). You don't need a global PM2 — use the `yarn` commands (`yarn logs`, `yarn restart`…), which always target the right daemon.

To start Loopar automatically after a server reboot, register the boot hook once:

```bash
yarn startup
```

---

## Installing Caddy

Caddy is required for production deployments with automatic SSL.

### Ubuntu/Debian

```bash
sudo apt install -y debian-keyring debian-archive-keyring apt-transport-https curl
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/gpg.key' | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/debian.deb.txt' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list
sudo apt update
sudo apt install caddy
```

### CentOS/RHEL/Fedora

```bash
sudo dnf install 'dnf-command(copr)'
sudo dnf copr enable @caddy/caddy
sudo dnf install caddy
```

### macOS

```bash
brew install caddy
```

### Windows

Download from [caddyserver.com/download](https://caddyserver.com/download) or use Chocolatey:

```powershell
choco install caddy
```

### Verify Installation

```bash
caddy version
# Output: v2.x.x
```

### Start Caddy as Service

```bash
# Linux (systemd)
sudo systemctl enable caddy
sudo systemctl start caddy

# Check status
sudo systemctl status caddy
```

> **Note:** Caddy is only required for production deployments. For local development, you can skip Caddy installation."},"imageProps":{},"style":{}},{"element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Setup Wizard","key":"md_setup_wizard","id":"setup-wizard","name":"md_setup_wizard","value":"# Install Wizard

The first time you open a new site, Loopar shows a step-by-step install wizard.

---

## Step 1: Database

Pick the database engine and the **server connection** (host, port, user, password). You don't name the database: the installer creates one for the site, with a name derived from your organization.

| Engine | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| **SQLite** | Zero configuration — a file under `sites/<site>/database/`. Ideal for development |
| **MySQL / MariaDB** | Production |
| **PostgreSQL** | Production, advanced features |
| **SQL Server / Oracle** | Existing Microsoft or Oracle infrastructure |

---

## Step 2: Organization

Your organization's name and basic details. They seed the **Company** record (identity, address, brand colors, currency, time zone), which letterheads and prints use later. You can complete it at any time from the Desk.

---

## Step 3: Administrator

The email and password of the **Administrator** account. The password must be strong.

---

## Completing Setup

When you click **Install**:

1. The database schema is created
2. The core app (`loopar`) and its data are installed
3. The Administrator user is created
4. You are taken to the Desk

If anything fails, the whole first install is **rolled back** and the wizard stays available — a site only counts as installed once its Administrator exists.

> **Installing on a remote server:** local and LAN installs open the wizard directly. When you install through the server's public IP or domain, the wizard needs the **install link** that `yarn start` (TUI) prints for the site — it carries a one-time token, so nobody else can take over a fresh site. After the install the token stops working.

> **Lost the Administrator password?** `yarn admin-reset <site> [email]` creates the Administrator or gives it a new temporary password.
"},"imageProps":{},"style":{}},{"element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Architecture Overview","key":"md_architecture","id":"architecture","name":"md_architecture","value":"# Architecture Overview

Loopar runs as **one Node process — the core** — that serves every site (tenant). Each request is routed to its tenant by host name; each tenant keeps its own database, configuration, users and domain.

![Loopar single-core multi-tenant architecture](/assets/public/home-multitenant.svg)

### Key Concepts

| Concept | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Core** | The single process (`loopar-core` in PM2) that owns the HTTP server and serves every tenant |
| **Tenant** | An independent site under `sites/<name>/` with its own database, config, users and domain |
| **dev site** | The default tenant, where you build apps and manage the others |
| **Mode** | `development` (Vite + HMR) or `production` (prebuilt bundle) — a **global** switch of the core, not per tenant |
| **PM2** | Keeps the core alive (project-local daemon) |
| **Caddy** | Routes every tenant domain to the core and handles SSL |

Because every tenant runs inside the same process, a code update reaches all of them at once, and turning a tenant on or off doesn't start or stop any process.
"},"imageProps":{},"style":{}},{"element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Project Structure","key":"md_project_structure","id":"project-structure","name":"md_project_structure","value":"# Project Structure

```
my-project/
├── apps/                    # Applications, shared by every tenant
│   └── loopar/              # The core app
│       ├── installer.json   # App manifest
│       ├── jobs.js          # Scheduled jobs (optional)
│       └── modules/
│           └── core/
│               ├── entities/<entity>/   # .json + model + controller + client/
│               ├── pages/<page>/
│               └── ...
├── config/
│   └── core.json            # Core settings: port, mode, host, Caddy, Redis
├── sites/                   # One folder per tenant
│   └── dev/
│       ├── config.json      # Tenant config: domain, status, websites, secrets
│       ├── config/
│       │   └── db.config.json   # Database connection
│       ├── database/        # SQLite file (when using SQLite)
│       ├── public/uploads/  # Tenant uploads
│       └── sessions/
├── backups/<tenant>/        # Tenant backups
├── build/releases/<tag>/    # Production builds (dist → current release)
├── packages/                # Framework workspace packages
│   ├── loopar/              # Core framework (server + client)
│   ├── db-env/              # Knex-based data layer
│   ├── server-env/          # Express + Socket.IO
│   └── ...                  # react-env, tailwind-env, markdown, shadcn…
├── bin/                     # cli/, tui/, build/, setup/
└── test/                    # unit/ and integration/ suites
```

### Key Directories

| Directory | Purpose |
|-----------|--------|
| `apps/` | Applications available to every tenant (installed per tenant) |
| `config/core.json` | Server-wide settings — nothing per tenant |
| `sites/<tenant>/` | Each tenant's configuration and data |
| `backups/` | Backup archives, one folder per tenant |
| `packages/` | Internal framework packages |

### File Types

| File | Purpose |
|------|--------|
| `<entity>.json` | Element definitions, metadata and structure |
| `<entity>.js` | Model — server-side business logic (optional) |
| `<entity>-controller.js` | Controller — HTTP actions (optional) |
| `client/<entity>-*.jsx` | Client-side React views (optional) |
| `sites/<t>/config.json` | Tenant configuration (older installs used `.env` — `yarn migrate` converts it) |
"},"imageProps":{},"style":{}},{"element":"markdown","data":{"label":"PM2 Commands","key":"md_pm2_commands","id":"pm2-commands","name":"md_pm2_commands","value":"# CLI & Process Management

Loopar ships a CLI that drives the core through a **project-local PM2 daemon**. The everyday commands:

```bash
yarn start          # open the TUI (and start the core if it is down)
yarn logs           # tail the logs
yarn restart        # restart the core
yarn tenant list    # tenants and their status
yarn build          # production build
yarn prod           # switch the core to production and boot
```

> **Mode is global.** Development (Vite + HMR) or production (prebuilt bundle) applies to the whole core — toggle it with `m` in the TUI or `yarn prod`.

The full list of commands and TUI keys is on the [CLI](/cli) page.
"},"imageProps":{},"style":{}},{"data":{"label":"Tenant Management","key":"md_tenant_management","id":"tenant-management","name":"md_tenant_management","value":"# Tenant Management

Tenants are managed from the **TUI** (`yarn start`) or from the **Tenant Manager** in the Desk of your dev site.

---

## Accessing Tenant Manager

1. Open `http://localhost:3000/desk`
2. Open **Tenant Manager** (or search it with `Ctrl/⌘ + K`)

---

## Creating a New Tenant

1. Click **New**
2. Fill in:
   - **Name** — unique identifier (e.g. `my-client`); it becomes `sites/my-client/`
   - **Domain** — optional: `my-client.localhost` locally, or a public domain
   - **Websites** — optional: extra domains served from this tenant (see the Website page)
3. Save, then **Open** the tenant: its install wizard creates the database, organization and Administrator

There is no port to choose: every tenant is served by the core on its single port and reached by host name (`my-client.localhost` works locally without DNS).

---

## Tenant Actions

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Open** | Open the tenant's Desk (or its install link if not installed) |
| **Start / Stop** | Turn the tenant on or off inside the core. Off tenants answer with a suspended page; nothing is deleted |
| **Restart** | Re-initialize the tenant (reloads its configuration and apps) |
| **Reset** | Wipe the tenant's database and start over from the install wizard |
| **Destroy** | Delete the tenant completely: its database, `sites/<name>/` and its Caddy route |
| **Core: Dev / Prod** | Switch the **whole core** between development and production |
| **Build / Deploy** | Full rebuild, or promote `build/staging` to a new live release |

---

## Tenant Lifecycle

```
Create → Install wizard → Build your apps → Assign a domain → Live (https://my-client.com)
                                                ↑
                                 one core, one mode for every tenant
```
"},"element":"markdown","imageProps":{},"style":{}},{"element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Production Deployment","key":"md_production","id":"production","name":"md_production","value":"# Production Deployment

---

## Prerequisites

1. **Caddy** installed and running on the server
2. Each tenant **domain pointing** to the server's IP
3. **Ports 80/443 open**

---

## Step 1: Build

```bash
yarn build
```

The build writes a versioned release under `build/releases/<tag>/` and swaps the `dist` symlink atomically — the previous release keeps serving until the new one is ready.

## Step 2: Switch the Core to Production

```bash
yarn prod
```

(or `m` in the TUI, or **Core: Prod** in the Tenant Manager). `yarn prod` refuses to switch when there is no build.

## Step 3: Assign Domains

In the Tenant Manager, set each tenant's **Domain** (e.g. `myapp.com`) and save. Loopar registers the domain in Caddy, which obtains the SSL certificate automatically.

## Step 4: Survive Reboots

```bash
yarn startup
```

---

## What Happens Behind the Scenes

```
browser ──https──► Caddy (:443, automatic SSL)
                     │  every tenant domain
                     ▼
                 Loopar core (one process, one port)
                     │  Host → tenant
          ┌──────────┼──────────┐
          ▼          ▼          ▼
       client-a   client-b   dev …   (own database, config, users)
```

---

## Production vs Development

| Aspect | Development | Production |
|--------|-------------|------------|
| Mode (`config/core.json` → `nodeEnv`) | `development` | `production` |
| Client code | Vite middleware + HMR | Prebuilt, compressed bundle |
| Debugger | On by default | Off unless `"debug": true` |
| Test runs from the Desk | Allowed | Disabled |
| Caddy | Tries `:80`, falls back to a free port | `:80` / `:443` or fails loudly |

The mode applies to **every tenant** at once: one core, one mode.

---

## Updating

```bash
git pull
yarn deps          # reproducible install, only when dependencies changed
yarn build
```

Then update each app from the **App Manager** of every tenant that uses it (schema changes are applied per tenant). A safety backup is taken before an app is installed or updated.
"},"imageProps":{},"style":{}},{"element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Troubleshooting","key":"md_troubleshooting","id":"troubleshooting","name":"md_troubleshooting","value":"# Troubleshooting

Common issues and their solutions.

---

## Yarn Version Issues

```
Error: This project requires Yarn 4+
```

**Solution:** Enable Yarn 4 through Corepack:

```bash
corepack enable
yarn set version stable
yarn --version
# Should output: 4.x.x
```

If an old global Yarn is shadowing the project version:

```bash
corepack enable
yarn set version stable
```

---

## The Core Doesn't Start

```bash
# See why
yarn logs loopar-core

# Is the port already in use?
lsof -i :3000

# Clean slate: kill the daemon and start again
yarn kill
yarn start
```

The TUI header shows the core state (`● server up` / `✖ server down`); press `c` to start it.

---

## Database Connection Failed

```
Error: Access denied for user 'root'@'localhost'
```

**Solutions:**

1. Verify database credentials in the setup wizard
2. Ensure the database server is running
3. Check that the database user has proper permissions:

```sql
CREATE DATABASE loopar_db;
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON loopar_db.* TO 'user'@'localhost';
FLUSH PRIVILEGES;
```

---

## `pm2` Not Found

You don't need a global PM2: it is a project dependency and Loopar runs its own daemon. Use `yarn logs`, `yarn restart`, `yarn stop`… instead of `pm2 …`. If `yarn` commands fail, run `yarn install` again.

---

## Caddy Not Registering Domain

```bash
# Check if Caddy is running
sudo systemctl status caddy

# Check Caddy logs
journalctl -u caddy -f

# Verify Admin API is accessible
curl http://localhost:2019/config/
```

**Common causes:**
- Caddy not running
- Port 2019 blocked
- Domain DNS not pointing to server

---

## SSL Certificate Not Generated

**Requirements for automatic SSL:**
- Domain must resolve to your server's IP
- Ports 80 and 443 must be open
- Caddy must be able to reach Let's Encrypt

```bash
# Test domain resolution
dig myapp.com

# Check if ports are open
sudo ufw status
```

---

## A Tenant Shows a "Suspended" Page

The tenant is turned off. Turn it on:

```bash
yarn tenant on my-site
```

or **Start** it from the Tenant Manager / TUI (`s`).

---

## Node Version Mismatch

```
Error: The engine "node" is incompatible
```

**Solution:** Loopar requires Node **22.22+**:

```bash
# Using nvm
nvm install 22
nvm use 22
nvm alias default 22
```

---

## Permission Errors (EACCES)

```
Error: EACCES: permission denied, open '...'
```

**Never fix this with `sudo`.** Loopar only writes inside your project folder and your user's home (pm2, Caddy storage) — a normal user already has all the access it needs. An `EACCES` almost always means a past `sudo` run left root-owned files behind, which breaks every later run without it.

Reclaim ownership instead of escalating:

```bash
# See what a past sudo run left behind
sudo find . -user root | head

# Take your files back (one time)
sudo chown -R "$(whoami)" .
sudo chown -R "$(whoami)" "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Caddy" 2>/dev/null
```

**Low ports without root:** macOS allows binding 80/443 unprivileged out of the box. On Linux, grant it to Caddy once:

```bash
sudo setcap 'cap_net_bind_service=+ep' $(which caddy)
```

Then always run `yarn start` / `yarn serve` as your normal user — never with `sudo`."},"imageProps":{},"style":{}},{"element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Next Steps","key":"md_next_steps","id":"next-steps","name":"md_next_steps","value":"# Next Steps

Congratulations! You have Loopar running. Here's what to explore next:

---

## Learn the Fundamentals

1. **[Concepts](/concepts)** — Understand Entities, Apps, Modules, and Builders
2. **[Learn](/learn)** — Step-by-step tutorials for building applications

---

## Build Your First App

1. Open `http://localhost:3000/desk`
2. Go to **App Manager** → **New**
3. Create your first Entity
4. Design its form by drag and drop
5. Open the auto-generated list — switch it to **Kanban** once you add a workflow

---

## Create Your First Tenant

1. Open **Tenant Manager** (or the TUI with `yarn start`)
2. Create a tenant and open it — its install wizard runs
3. Install your app on the tenant from its App Manager
4. When ready, assign a domain and deploy to production

---

## Explore the Desk

The sidebar groups modules **by app** (the rail on the left); each app can have its own home page. Press **Ctrl/⌘ + K** anywhere to jump to any list, form, page or record.

| Section | Purpose |
|---------|--------|
| **App Manager** | Create, install and update applications |
| **Entity** | Define data models and views |
| **Page Builder** | Build public web pages |
| **Desk Page / Dashboard** | Build app home pages and dashboards |
| **Tenant Manager** | Create and manage tenants |
| **System Settings / Company** | System configuration and organization identity |

---

## Join the Community

- ⭐ Star us on [GitHub](https://github.com/alphabit-technology/loopar-framework)
- 🐛 Report issues or request features
- 🤝 Contribute to the project

---

> **Tip:** The best way to learn Loopar is by building. Start with a simple app in the dev site, then create a tenant and deploy it. The visual environment makes it easy to experiment!"},"imageProps":{},"style":{}}],"imageProps":{},"style":{}}]
